title: microcap-hiring-prio-matrix-and-7-day-integration-slate
content:
Purpose and scope:
Quick, pragmatic playbook for sourcing and onboarding "microcap" hires — defined as headcount to deliver a scoped 4–8 week project (temp-to-hire or short fixed-term IC). Goal: reduce time-to-impact and hiring overhead while maintaining decision quality.

High-level goals:
- Get deliverable owner into productive flow within 7 days.
- Keep interview loop to 2–3 focused evaluators.
- Use a lightweight rubric to surface risk signals early.
- Document decisions and clear fallback plan if ramp misses targets.

When to use this flow (signals):
- Project < 8 weeks with clear acceptance criteria
- Budget constrained — small headcount or contractor budget
- Need immediate hands-on contributor (not manager)
- Role scope well-scoped with measurable output (examples: data pipeline patch, evaluation harness build, infra runbook automation)

Priority matrix (quick triage) — score 1–5 each, total max 20:
- Impact urgency (1 low — 5 critical)
- Replacement difficulty (1 easy — 5 niche/specialist)
- Ramp tolerance (1 long ramp OK — 5 must be fast)
- External candidate funnel depth (1 deep — 5 sparse)

Interpretation notes:
- 16–20: Fast-track hire (aim 7–14 day fill)
- 11–15: Standard micro-hire (14–21 day fill)
- <=10: Re-evaluate need or expand scope to longer term hire

Interview loop design (lean):
1) Recruiter phone screen (30m) — confirm experience match, candidates' availability, comp range, and must-have technical example.
2) Practical short-live exercise (take-home or pair session, 60–90m) — single milestone: reproduce small piece of infra or implement a small evaluation script. Keep grading checklist.
3) One technical deep-dive + culture fit (45m) — interviewer focuses on problem-solving and past similar projects.
Optional: brief hiring manager sync (15m) to confirm decision.

Rapid rubric (use for both take-home + interview). Scores 1–5, add notes:
- Core competency (domain knowledge): anchors: 5 = shipped relevant system solo, 3 = helped on team, 1 = theoretical only
- Problem decomposition: 5 = clean plan + edge-cases; 3 = workable but misses some edges; 1 = struggles to break down
- Execution speed / pragmatism: 5 = tradeoffs + delivery-first; 3 = decent; 1 = over-architects
- Communication & async docs: 5 = concise tickets + README habit; 3 = ok; 1 = poor
- Risk signals (reverse scoring, 1 = green, 5 = red): copy/paste or boilerplate answers, missing fundamentals, evasive on tradeoffs

Decision threshold (recommended):
- Total technical score (first four items) average >= 3.5 AND risk signals <=2 -> proceed.
- If borderline (avg 3.0–3.5) -> hire on probationary 30d contract with explicit goals.
- If <3.0 -> reject.

Sample take-home grading checklist (quick):
- Does solution run? (yes/no)
- Meets core acceptance criteria? (yes/partial/no)
- Clear README + instructions? (yes/no)
- Obvious security or scale anti-patterns? (flagged/none)
- Time spent (candidate self-report)

7-day integration slate (targeted onboarding to first PR):
Pre-boarding (before day0) — recruiter / ops tasks:
- Ensure account created (git, slack, jira) and access request submitted (IT ticket template).
- Send a 1-page project brief + acceptance criteria + sample data where applicable.
- First-week calendar: pair sessions, doc time, sync with mentor.

Day0 — orientation (~2 hrs):
- People ops welcome + payroll/contract checklist (30m)
- Setup dev environment walkthrough with pairing (60–90m)
- Quick 15m intro to team priorities and OKR slice

Day1 — alignment & small win plan:
- Review project brief and deliverable for week (30m)
- Identify the 1st small win (bug fix, script, test) and get it merged ideally by EOD
- Document blockers and escalate path

Day2–3 — focused execution:
- Pair sessions with mentor 2x 45m
- Daily async standup note in thread (one-line status)

Day4 — review checkpoint:
- 30m sync to review progress on first milestone
- Update acceptance criteria if needed

Day5–7 — wrap & iterate:
- Ship first PR, postmortem note (what worked, what blocked)
- Week1 retro with hiring manager (15m) and conversion/next-steps decision

Fail-fast triggers (examples):
- Unable to run local environment by end of Day1 without reasonable blockers
- No visible code or docs produced by Day4
- Communication gaps that create risk to delivery (missed check-ins, unclear replies)

Probation/30d contract guardrails (if used):
- Clear deliverables with acceptance criteria and success metrics (tickets assigned)
- Weekly checkpoints + final decision at day30 (convert, extend, or offboard)
- Compensation benchmark: align to market + pro-rated benefits notes

Interview debrief template (copy into candidate thread):
- Candidate: [name] | role applied: [role] | loop date:
- Quick summary (2 lines):
- Strengths (bullets):
- Concerns / risk flags (bullets):
- Technical score (avg): [#] /5
- Recommend: Hire / Probation-contract / No-hire (circle)
- Notes for offer (salary band / start date / contract length)

Open questions & TODOs (working list):
- Confirm standard contract template for 30d probation with legal (action: Sana)
- Build an automated pre-boarding checklist in HRIS to reduce manual steps (ticket: JIRA-3921)
- Create one-page project brief template for hiring managers (Luis to draft)

Notes to self / heuristics: 
- Keep loops small; avoid heavyweight onsite for microcap roles
- Use take-homes oriented around company infra to reduce ramp time (even if smaller scope)
- Always ship a first-PR goal — that outcome tells more than coding tests

References and links:
- Confluence: peopleops/microcap-hire-template (draft)
- Slack thread: #people-ops-hiring (pin: sample take-home)
- Jira: JIRA-3921 (preboarding automation)

Quick version history:
- 2025-10-03 initial notes and matrix
- 2025-11-15 added 7-day slate and debrief template

End of doc.
